readMe: ONE ARTIFACT, TWO CONSUMERS. The cloud coordinator reads this to know what has
been settled; the local sim session reads it to know what to run next.
`bin/make-promotion-batch.js` turns it into the next batch's spec files, so
'what should the PC run next?' is a command and not a judgement call.
THE ONE RULE THIS LEDGER EXISTS TO ENFORCE: a deterministic probe is NECESSARY
AND NEVER SUFFICIENT. CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED passed its deterministic ship gate
outright (fatal stagings 41 -> 0) and then lost snake6 1.00 -> 0.15 live, through
exhaustion — a travel-economy channel the probe does not measure. Only a live
paired sweep, with a concurrent verified null and a VERIFIED ENGAGED treatment
arm, may write a live status.

statusLadder: dark -> probe-passed  : a deterministic probe cleared its gate. Goes no further.
probe-passed -> live-* : only a live paired sweep with a verified concurrent null.
supported -> promoted  : the default flip was actually made; `promotedBy` names the commit.
frozen                 : re-opened by a MECHANISM CLAIM only, never by a p-value.
explorationSliceRule: A promoted or supported flag keeps ~10% of its cells running the OPPOSITE branch,
forever. Today's policy selects tomorrow's corpus, so a cell that turned a flag on
will otherwise never generate the data by which it could be turned back off.
powerArithmetic: A block is one seed through every cyclic seat rotation (3 games on a 3-team board).
Placement: 80% power at MDE 0.25 needs ~58 blocks on the pooled stratum, 8 on the
tightest (mix23 alone); MDE 0.10 needs 362-1,447. That is 360-1,000+ games per cell
PER ARM. Mechanism metrics move at n~8 blocks and are 5-25x outside the null band.
So: refit on mechanism, describe placement, and refuse a placement verdict from a
cell whose blocksHad < blocksNeeded. (A3 memo section 4.1.)
retiredCounters: plansEvaluated and boundsInversions are RETIRED as verdict-bearing metrics on any
live arm: at any budget they are dominated by how much CPU the process got. They
carry a verdict ONLY under a fixed-tick StepClock A/A, where the arms consume
identical work by construction. They are still reported, because they diagnose a
armEngagementRule: A live measurement must carry armEngagementVerified. `false` records the row and
moves nothing: a null from an arm that never ran is a different finding from a null
from an arm that ran and did not help. P5 is the standing exhibit — CENTAUR_WASM is
refused per partition, silently, whenever an input is not resident in linear memory.
CL7's mechanism report (TeamTurnResult.mechanism) is what makes the answer readable.

Applied literally that voids every verdict in batch 1. THE LEDGER DOES NOT APPLY IT LITERALLY HERE, and says why: 4 thrown decisions in 195,000+ is a rate of 2e-5, the four sit in four unrelated arms with no shared cell or bundle, and none is in the null pair. What it does void is the CLAIM of zero. flagValueAudit.question: Commit 38e15e7 warns that every CL flag parses only `1|on|true` with no warning on a typo. The batch's envAtRun stamps read "1" for the CL flags but "on" for CENTAUR_WASM and CENTAUR_COHORT_POLICY and "full" for CENTAUR_TIER_TRUTH. Did any arm silently run its own baseline?
flagValueAudit.answer: NO. Checked value by value against each flag's own `parses` field in this ledger. CENTAUR_COHORT_POLICY parses `1|on|true`, so "on" is in its set. CENTAUR_WASM parses `on|off`, so "on" is its ONLY on-value. CENTAUR_TIER_TRUTH parses `off|expiry|full`, so "full" is correct. The `1|on|true` warning applies to the five search-side CL flags, all of which were set to "1". Sixteen arms audited, zero mistyped.

flags.verdict: DO NOT PROMOTE AS-IS — and the failure is SNAKE-DENSITY-DEPENDENT, not global. The deterministic gate passed and the live arm collapsed through a channel the gate does not measure. But the collapse is confined to the cells with few or no pieces: on null-snake6 the seed loses 1.00 -> 0.15, while on headline-mix-king placement is flat and two mechanism rows (finalMaterial +5.10 ✱, survived +0.146 ✱) run in its FAVOUR. Exhaustion inflation is present everywhere the snakes outnumber the pieces (x2.09 knight, x1.92 snake6, x1.19 mix-king) but only converts into a placement loss where there is no piece play to absorb it. The live reading is therefore not "the seed is a dead idea" but "the seed is admissible on some boards and ruinous on others, and nothing currently decides which board it is on". That points at a CONDITIONAL ADMISSION future — the same shape CENTAUR_STAGING_SAFETY already ships as `auto` after helping on piece boards and regressing on snake-only — and NOT at a retirement. The status stays live-failed and the ledger's own rule is why: a failure is undone by a root cause and a repaired arm, never by other cells declining to reproduce it. The piece-cell rows are the beginning of a root cause, not a second opinion. MACHINE INGEST, 20260829 — every transcribed number reproduces exactly, and the per-game rows sharpen the mechanism in three ways the aggregates could not. (1) EXHAUSTION IS A MINORITY OF THE DAMAGE: on null-snake6 the seed loses 260 units per 48 games against cl-off's 53 (x4.91), while replay-mined exhaustion goes 39 -> 75 (x1.92) — 185 of the 260 died of something the exhaustion headline does not name, which is a constraint on any root cause. (2) ON THE PIECE CELL IT CHANGES THE CAUSE MIX, NOT THE AMOUNT: snake5-knight total unit loss is flat (209 -> 215) while exhaustion doubles, and on headline-mix-king total loss FALLS (163 -> 137). That is the density-dependence stated mechanically. (3) IT IS A GRIND: median elimination turn 98 of a 120 cap, nothing before turn 30, and the losing games are the LONGER ones — so the `turns -9.98` row is a change in terminal KIND, not "dies earlier". Per block, all 16 snake6 seeds are hurt and none is spared, while snake5-knight is two populations cancelling (4 hurt, 8 flat, 4 helped). A root cause must predict which board is which. SOURCE-LEVEL RECONCILIATION, 20260829 — THE REJECT STANDS AND THE MECHANISM IS TWO CHANNELS, NOT ONE. Channel A is travel economy, and it is now sourced: the seed's objective is three repulsive de-confliction terms (same-cell contest, edge exchange, team-mate's body by tier) plus ONE weak attractor (follow-the-tail, capped at 0.06), and it contains NO food term and NO travel-cost term at all — so on a board where every unit is on a starvation clock, a purely spatial objective spends health, and exhaustion death here is death by movement cost (`turnEngine.ts:92`, `Game.ts:205`, food as the rescue). That channel is 29% of the damage. Channel B is UNEXTRACTED and larger: of the 207 extra units the seed loses on null-snake6, only 36 are extra exhaustions. `ClashKind` (`Game.ts:199-208`) enumerates contest · edge · bodyBlock · sever · hazard · exhaustion · wall · self · regicide; on that cell hazards are off and there is no king, which leaves contest, edge, bodyBlock, wall and self — EXACTLY THE COLLISION CHANNEL THE CL1 SHIP CRITERION CERTIFIED AS FIXED (fatal stagings 41 -> 0 scattered and 64 -> 8 confronted, team-mate kills 25 -> 4). So the seed's central OFFLINE safety result appears not to have transferred to live play, which is a sharper indictment than the exhaustion headline and is a hard constraint on P7R: a root cause that explains only exhaustion explains under a third of the deaths on the cell where the seed collapses. PROCESS FINDING: the ship criterion gated on fatal stagings, a DIFFERENT death channel from the one that killed it, so any future seed/ordering flag must be gated on a CAUSE-OF-DEATH BREAKDOWN and not on stagings alone. PIECE-GATED ADMISSION — REJECTED, 20260829: DO NOT BUILD IT. The BOARD-LEVEL form of the conditional-admission reading above ("admit the seed only on piece-bearing boards") is falsified by a cell already in this batch. `snake5-knight` IS piece-bearing and would pass any board-level piece gate, and there the seed delivers exhaustion x2.09 (23 -> 48, the worst ratio in the batch), subject-team eliminations 1/48 -> 6/48, ratchet per decision +0.01026 ✱ (the largest in the batch — the seed's plan sticking), worstWallMs +4.29 ms ✱ — and score NULL (-0.0104 [-0.142, +0.121]). Full price, zero benefit. The piece-cell "win" on headline-mix-king does not carry the gate either: finalMaterial +5.10 [+0.44, +9.77] and survived +0.146 [+0.001, +0.290] are DIRECTION-ONLY — both lower bounds sit within 0.5 of zero, neither has a cell-local A/A floor, and that cell decorrelates completely under ZERO treatment (A/A 5 of 48 games identical in length, turn-correlation -0.193), so its per-game statistics carry far less information than n=48 suggests. The gate the mechanism implies is PER-UNIT, not per-board — the harm is a travel-economy cost borne by trail units while the benefit is de-confliction among units that contest cells, and the codebase already separates them — but the seed's ONLY positive term, follow-the-tail, is itself a trail-unit term, so a per-unit gate is a real design question with a plausible failure mode and not a one-liner. Order of work, cheapest first: re-mine the existing replays for the full ClashKind breakdown (free, no new games — and until it is done any fix is aimed at 29% of the problem), then a health-aware travel-economy term in ψ, then a per-unit gate with its own arm. STATUS UNCHANGED BY THIS PARAGRAPH: live-failed stands, and the ledger's own rule is why — a failure is undone by a root cause and a repaired arm, never by a design idea.

findings.id: the seed does not lose battles, it loses the team
findings.detail: On `null-snake6`, cl-off and cl-fatality end 48 of 48 games with the subject team ALIVE (mean 4.90 and 4.92 units of 6 surviving). cl-seed is eliminated in 27 of 48 and ends with a mean of 0.58 units; 27 of its 48 games end with ZERO units and 16 more with one. cl-both: 25 of 48, mean 0.71.

findings.id: exhaustion explains under a third of the damage
findings.detail: Total units lost per 48 games on null-snake6: cl-off 53, cl-seed 260 -- x4.91. The replay-mined exhaustion count over the same games is 39 -> 75, x1.92. So exhaustion accounts for 74% of cl-off's losses and only 29% of cl-seed's: 185 of the seed's 260 lost units died of something the exhaustion headline does not name. THIS IS A CONSTRAINT ON P7R: a root cause that explains only exhaustion explains less than a third of the deaths on the cell where the seed collapses.

findings.id: on the piece cell the seed changes the cause mix, not the amount
findings.detail: On `snake5-knight` total units lost is FLAT -- cl-off 209, cl-seed 215 (x1.03) -- while exhaustion doubles, 23 -> 48 (x2.09). The seed substitutes exhaustion deaths for other deaths without changing how many units die, and placement reads null. That is a much sharper statement than "x2.09 inflation on a cell whose placement is null" and it is the strongest single argument for the conditional-admission reading. On `headline-mix-king` the seed REDUCES total unit loss, 163 -> 137 (x0.84), while exhaustion rises 16 -> 19 -- the same substitution, with the trade landing in its favour. SUPERSEDED IN PART, 20260829: this is an argument for CONDITIONAL admission and NOT for the BOARD-LEVEL form of it. The same cell falsifies a piece gate — score NULL while ratchet per decision runs +0.01026 ✱, worstWallMs +4.29 ms ✱ and subject-team eliminations go 1/48 -> 6/48, i.e. full price and no benefit. See the verdict's PIECE-GATED ADMISSION paragraph.

findings.id: it is a grind, not a blunder
findings.detail: Turn of elimination on null-snake6 under cl-seed: median 98 of a 120 cap, quartiles 54/108, range 30-119. 15 of the 27 eliminations happen after turn 90 and only 8 before turn 60; NOTHING happens before turn 30. cl-both is slightly earlier (median 82). A travel-economy story fits this; a single early fatal staging does not.

findings.id: the fold's "dies earlier" gloss is wrong at the per-game level
findings.detail: turns -9.979 [-15.499, -4.459] was read as "dies earlier". Per game: cl-off games run to the cap (median 120, cap rate 0.938); cl-seed games END, at a median of 118 turns, because a team is gone. cl-seed's LOSSES are its LONGER games (median 118) and its wins are its shorter ones (median 100). The aggregate turns delta is a change in terminal KIND, not in how long the subject survives. The `decisive +0.4792` row is the same fact stated correctly: endKind on null-snake6 goes from 45 cap / 3 last-team-standing under cl-off to 22 cap / 26 last-team-standing under cl-seed.

findings.id: the damage is total on snake6 and board-specific on the knight cell
findings.detail: Per-block (per-seed) subject score, cl-seed minus cl-off: on null-snake6 ALL 16 blocks are hurt, from -0.333 to -0.833, with none unchanged and none helped -- no board is spared, so there is no pathological-seed story. nextExperiment.designNote: SCORED ON THROUGHPUT, NOT ON PLACEMENT — and that is a correction to the spec, not a preference. `src/lobster/wasm/differential.test.ts` asserts that `on.rows` equals `off.rows`, and that a REFUSED kernel degrades to the same answer rather than a wrong one; `policy.ts` states it in words — the JS path is the source of truth, so `on` is never a correctness bet, it is a THROUGHPUT bet. The arm is therefore bit-exact BY CONSTRUCTION AND BY TEST and cannot move a placement metric: `score`, `win` and `place` are null BY DESIGN here. They are read out as description and they score nothing. Scoring a throughput flag on win rate is a category error and it comes out of this spec. WHAT IS SCORED, in order: (1) the ENGAGEMENT RATE per cell, wasmRuns/(wasmRuns+wasmRefused); (2) PLANS PER DECISION, `plansEvaluated_RETIRED` over `decisions`, and decisions per second at a fixed budget; (3) `worstWallMs`. AND DO NOT QUIETLY UNDO THE RETIREMENT: `plansEvaluated` is a RETIRED verdict metric (conventions.retiredCounters) because at any budget it is dominated by how much CPU the process got, and normalising per decision does not repair that by itself. It carries a verdict HERE only if BOTH conditions hold — the two arms are launched SIMULTANEOUSLY so they share one machine-weather, and the A/A null measures a floor for the SAME statistic on the SAME cell. The exhibit is in batch 1: its A/A pair swung plans per decision by +65% on `headline-mix-king` under zero treatment, which is what an unfloored throughput number is worth. FLOOR EVERY SCORED STATISTIC ON EVERY SCORED CELL. THE ALTERNATIVE THE EVIDENCE ALLOWS is raising THAT CELL'S n by ~4x, and it is not taken: blocks are a property of the SPEC and not of a cell, so this generator cannot express a per-cell n without a code change, and the spec-wide version would spend four times the box time on the batch's least informative board to buy back its least informative rows. openInstrumentItems.what: THE LEDGER HAS NOWHERE TO RECORD HOW MUCH A CELL CAN MEASURE, so no rule can refuse a row for being asked on a board that cannot answer it. `headline-mix-king` — the batch's headline board, and the cell the wasm anomaly is reported on — is trajectory-unstable under ZERO treatment: the A/A null flips 26 of 48 placements between two builds of the SAME commit (54%), only 5 of 48 games come out identical, the paired turn-correlation is -0.193, A/A plans-per-decision swings +65%, and across 14 arm-sweeps of the identical configHash 3749a5dea5e82e99 the cap rate spans 0.229-0.458 (mean 0.306, sd 0.060) — batch 1's two wasm arms being exactly the minimum and the maximum of that spread. Pairing by seed buys NO variance reduction there. THE DESIGN QUESTION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ITEM IS FOR AND ALL IT IS FOR: where should cell quality LIVE so that rules can consume it — a block on the batch record, a field on the A/A null's own rows, or a table the ingest derives and the generator reads — and WHICH RULES should it feed: refuse a placement verdict outright, require a larger n, or disqualify the cell from a spec at generation time? NOT DECIDED HERE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. No `batches[].cellQuality` machinery was invented for it: the schema should follow the decision rather than lead it, and inventing a channel now would commit the loop to whichever of the three shapes happened to be easiest to write.
openInstrumentItems.impact: Two-sided, and both sides are already in this ledger without being sayable. (1) EVERY PLACEMENT ROW ON THAT CELL IS NULL BY CONSTRUCTION. A 54% A/A placement-flip rate is what a +/-0.0973 score floor looks like in games, so the batch's headline board cannot carry a placement claim at n=48 — the rows recorded on it are honest and uninformative rather than wrong, and reading them as 'the treatment did nothing' overstates them. (2) NOTHING REPORTED THIS. The `flip-rate-rose` event fires only when the paired flip rate RISES against a previous batch, and batch 1 is the first batch, so a first-order fact about what the headline cell can measure passed through the whole instrument table in silence. That is FLIP-RATE-LEVEL seen from the data side rather than the rule side. By contrast `null-snake6` is stable — A/A 44 of 48 identical, and the order-preserving CENTAUR_UNIT_FATALITY holds trajectory correlation at +0.912 — which is exactly why P7's verdict on that cell stands while P5's on the mix-king cell does not. The quality of a cell is currently something a reader has to know; it should be something a rule can read.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: Taken where it costs nothing and is defensible one cell at a time: P5R drops `headline-mix-king` on this measured disqualification (see CENTAUR_WASM.nextExperiment.scopeNote), and every row is already read against its own cell's A/A floor since NULL-BAND-CELL-KEY closed, so an unreadable cell at least reads as unreadable. What is NOT available is the general form — the next flag to ask a placement question on that board gets the same null, and nothing in the rules will say why.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: the owner's decision on the design question above, then a schema field and one rule that consumes it. FLIP-RATE-LEVEL needs a second batch to calibrate a level threshold against and batch 2 supplies one, so the two should be settled together at the next ingest rather than separately — a level threshold on the A/A cell IS a cell-quality number, and deciding where it lives is deciding where they both live.

standingExperiments.title: The budget ladder
standingExperiments.approvedBy: owner — pre-approved, conditional on budget-probe v2 confirming
standingExperiments.trigger: CONFIRMED, and here is the whole arithmetic. budget-probe v2, 60 recorded positions drawn from 480 integrated replays, idle box, FRESH ENGINE PER POSITION, sample seed 1, 9 skipped: a true 1000 ms run reproduces the 2000 ms decision on 55 of 60 positions. FLIPS 5/60 = 8.3% (+/-7.0). A/A FLOOR, 2000 ms against itself: 1/60 = 1.7% (+/-3.2). EXCESS ATTRIBUTABLE TO BUDGET = 6.7 points, wide at n=60 and the intervals overlap — the direction is clear and the magnitude is not. The condition on the owner's pre-approval is met.
standingExperiments.question: Where on the budget curve does the substrate stop being speed and start being strength? P1 found the perf substrate was speed-not-strength at 2000 ms; the bimodal revision result (65% of decisions settle by 250 ms, 34.8% revise in a wave at 1000-1500 ms, nothing between) says 1000 ms would amputate the second pass entirely. Three points draw the line.
standingExperiments.designNote: ONE trail-instrumented cell in the ladder. The 35% revision wave was measured PRE-CL3, and cluster enumeration front-loads coordination, so the wave's own shape may have moved — which would make the ladder's middle rung mean something different from what it meant last month. Mechanism-first at 8 blocks: placement is descriptive here, not claimable. BATCH-1 NOTE: the 500 ms rung is now the interesting one. If the deep pass lands at 1000-1500 ms and the engine reschedules it under a 1 s budget, then 1000 ms may barely differ from 2000 ms while 500 ms amputates the pass outright — so the ladder's information is concentrated at its bottom rung.
standingExperiments.caveat: CHANGED != IMPROVED, and nothing measures the difference. The 35.0%/60.1% figures count decisions whose staged move-set changed; the 8.3% counts decisions a shorter budget decides differently. Whether those ~7% are BETTER is unmeasured and is exactly what the ladder is for.
standingExperiments.reconciliation: TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT LOOK LIKE THEY DISAGREE, AND DO NOT. The emission trails say 35.0% (P4, 50,455 decisions) and 60.1% (P5, 52,191) of decisions differ from what was staged at 1000 ms. budget-probe v2 says a true 1 s budget reproduces the 2 s decision 91.7% of the time. Both are right. The last-emission histogram shows the engine stages an incumbent in under 250 ms in 99.9% of decisions and then either never revises or revises in a single wave landing at 1000-1500 ms — the 250-1000 ms window is EMPTY, 8 decisions out of 102,646. The engine is deadline-aware: under a 1 s budget it RESCHEDULES the deep pass rather than losing it. So "what was on the table at 1000 ms" and "what a 1000 ms engine decides" are different questions, and only the second is the one the ladder asks. Net: the second second changes about 7% of decisions.
standingExperiments.retracted: budget-probe v1 IS RETRACTED — DO NOT INGEST. It reused one engine across games, and engines carry per-game ledger state, so its results were degenerate (0/60 flips in 26 s). Fixed in 65aa973. If a v1 file turns up in the archive, it is not evidence.
